characters/k'in-ch'ak.html.title: K'in Ch'ak
characters/k'in-ch'ak.html.description:
K'in Ch'ak is a Human Cleric living in the farming town of Brunea in Brun. They manage one of the larger maize silos in town, keeping records of harvests, trade, and can always be trusted to know everything that goes in and out of the silo by his huge ledger with exact details of every grain of maize.
K'in's almost obsessive recording stems from his regular amnesia, which had grown so bad that he doesn't even remember his childhood for the most part or any of his family. His most prominent memory is of waking up out in the fields with a single large jade stone in his mouth, which he wore about his neck from that moment forward as his artefact.The focus of K'in's spirituality is the bevelled, almost glowing green of the giant jade gemstone strung around his neck by a simple piece of twine.He believes that all things that happen to him are a result of the power of this artefact, and that it is his sole duty to protect it and follow it's "wishes". The stone, of course, makes no noise, nor does it communicate to K'in in any describable way, but he feels that the very foundation of his morals and being is tied to the stone, and as such, what he feels is right is the Will Of The Stone.The accountant-cleric also uses the stone as a way of explaining away the unexplainable. His lack of appetite for the very crops he's responsible for maintaining, the strange appearance of mud on his boots in the morning when they were spotless the evening before, the dried blood that occasionally appeared in his moustache... Will Of The Stone. Nothing more.K'in is ostracised greatly from his community. His apparent lack of family or existing friends, and general "weirdness" drove people away, preferring to stay within their cliques instead of risk being friends with the weird pale man who lived in the maize silo.He spends the majority of his life engrossed in his work, ignoring the world around him and only focusing on the numbers, the data, the science of maize. This was what the stone wanted, he told himself. There's nothing in the world that could be more important than maximising the throughput of this silo, that's his purpose in life as things currently stand.
Whistle? "Often, whistles carved from rocks into the shapes of gods or animals were included in the grave offerings to help the deceased find their way to Xibalba (She-BALba).". Could have the whistle be non-functional to signify that he was unable to make his way to Xibalba, hence still being here.Relatively young, about 25The Jade Stone has this carved on it. Yum Cimil, lord of death

Maya death god (God A, Xibalba, etc.) in the lunar eclipse tables of the Dresden Codex

equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.21-the-m.title: 1.21 The Maquaana Empire
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.21-the-m.description: The Maquaana Empire is the greatest power on the continent, having rapidly expanded outwards from its original place in the south-east of Afarsti. Its population is largely made up of Pinchinchu, but there is diversity, especially as the inhabitants of colonised areas are subsumed into the Maqua. The Maqua are an incredibly proud people, owed mostly to their faith in both the legendary figure of Ramaq (see 2.41) and their Emperors, the God-Kings. They follow an expansionist ideology and believe they are uniting the continent. They have become significantly less brutal with their enemies in the past 20 years, following the particularly bloody war with the Bailow, but still pose a force to be reckoned with. The Maqua capital, Zaada, is a hotspot for technology, science, art and commerce, being the biggest city in the continent. It also hosts the Imperial Temple, a grand building that seasonally houses the imperial family.
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.21-the-m.sourcePath: Equator/1. World/1.2 Factions/1.21 The Maquaana Empire.md

equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.22-the-b.title: 1.22 The Brun
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.22-the-b.description:
The Brun are a relatively traditional society situated to the west of the continent. Their population is mixed between Brux and other species, e.g. Pinchinchu, Ger, Human and Pluri. They have a strong spiritual system (see 1.42) which creates a unique social class for craftspeople as religious figures. The Brun are governed by councils of village and town leaders, and the laws differ by region. 1.42 Brun Spirituality
The Brun believe that certain objects can possess metaphysical abilities. This can range from artefacts to locations, modern and ancient. Crafts are sacred and craftspeople are viewed as sage-like figures. Most Brun will carry a significant object made by said craftspeople for the duration of their lives, often an object associated with their choice of work or lifestyle, for example a weapon, a tool or a figurine. This object is acquired from a Brun craftsperson at the age of 16 and buried alongside its holder. The power that every Brun artefact holds collectively is called Maur. Some Brun see Maur as an entity, but the most popular belief is that Maur is made up of the souls of Brun ancestors. Brun artefacts are revered for their quality and power, although a non-Brun has never been known to be able to harness Maur. There is an issue of grave robbing at Brun burial sites, especially the tombs of famous Brun, so the Brun burial system has advanced so that the actual burial site is somewhat removed from any monument. Despite this, thievery of Brun artefacts is still a prominent issue. During skirmishes, Maqua soldiers have been known to take Brun artefacts as trophies.

equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.23-the-d.title: 1.23 The Dailow
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.23-the-d.description: The Dailow are a people tormented by their recent past. Once a proud and powerful nation situated to the east of Afarsti, the Dailow were forced upwards into the mountains in a bloody war with the Maqua. Many left their families, homes and livelihoods behind. Those who stayed to fight were slain or worse. These days, the Dailow live in fear of the Maqua’s advance, situated in the mountains. It boasts a highly trained, deadly militia. The Dailow are a people tormented by their recent past. Once a proud and powerful nation situated to the east of Afarsti, the Dailow were forced upwards into the mountains in a bloody war with the Maqua. Many left their families, homes and livelihoods behind. Those who stayed to fight were slain or worse. These days, the Dailow live in fear of the Maqua’s advance, situated in the mountains. It boasts a highly trained, deadly militia. Their population is largely human, and they can be distrusting of Pinchinchu, as many have memories of the foul acts committed during the war. There are a few other races that have integrated into their society, particularly some of the Carsa, who inhabited the mountains before the Dailow arrived.

equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.24-grent.title: 1.24 Grentia
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.24-grent.description: Grentia is a relatively small nation situated to the center-south of the continent. It operates from its capital, Faje, through an elected leader. It is mostly populated by Silt. It is a country well-known for its wealth and cultural richness, and is known to stay fairly neutral in conflict. It has fairly good relations with the Maqua due to their trade, but many believe that Grentia is just afraid of the empire.

equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.25-the-n.title: 1.25 The Naokari Wetlands
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.25-the-n.description: The Naokari Wetlands exist in the south-west corner of the continent. They are mostly wild, with sparse villages and towns scattered across them. These villages are self-governing.
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.25-the-n.sourcePath: Equator/1. World/1.2 Factions/1.25 The Naokari Wetlands.md

equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.26-other.title: 1.26 Other settlements
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.26-other.description: There are various small clan and village groups in Afarsti, too many to write here. Please let me know if you have any questions or ideas about settlements!

equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.211-mara.title: 1.211 Mara, The God-King
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.211-mara.description: The current Emperor of the Maqua is Mara Maqua Chajiku, He Who The Sun Looks Upon. He is young, only 14 when his father was assassinated 8 years ago, and much less brutal to enemies than his predecessor, Yand, but has nonetheless continued the path of expansion for the empire. Right now, there are extreme tensions between the Brun and the Maqua, verging on war, following the capture of an ancestral Brun site by the Maqua.
equator/1.-world/1.2-factions/1.211-mara.sourcePath: Equator/1. World/1.2 Factions/1.211 Mara, The God-King.md

equator/1.-world/1.4-faith/1.41-ramaq,-m.title: 1.41 Ramaq, Mother and Mind
equator/1.-world/1.4-faith/1.41-ramaq,-m.description: Ramaq is thought of as much as a historical figure as she is as a religious one. According to Maqua mythology, she was a being made of pure light, born of a dragon and a moonray. Such was her beauty that Ramaq was beloved by the earth itself. Her will became that which was, as the earth bent to her will. She crumbled a great, domineering empire, and in its place established the Maquaana Empire. On the day that she died, she came to the top of the temple her people had built for her, raised her hands to the sky and told her people that hereafter, she shall be married to the sun, and that if her people walked in its light she would look upon them always. She promptly died and her remains are kept on that spot to this day, entombed in a golden statue. To this day, Maquaana proudly asserts itself as the Only Nation Under the Sun. The God-King line is said to have been born of a fallen star, the children of Ramaq and the sun itself. The line has not been entirely preserved by blood, with several of its heirs being killed or dying prematurely, but there are certain secretive rites in which a hatchling can be acknowledged as an heir to continue the line.
equator/1.-world/1.4-faith/1.41-ramaq,-m.sourcePath: Equator/1. World/1.4 Faith/1.41 Ramaq, Mother and Mind.md

equator/1.-world/1.4-faith/1.43-the-dail.title: 1.43 The Dailow
equator/1.-world/1.4-faith/1.43-the-dail.description: The Dailow once worshiped a god, but that was long ago. Now, the Dailow belief system is more of an unspoken code of conduct. Protect your family and kin, and know yourself.When the Dailow first left their home, they were forced to abandon the graves and tombs of their loved ones and ancestors. On the long road north, they could not bury their dead for the knowledge that the Maqua would claim their graves as territory. From this, a new burial system emerged in which bodies are sent adrift in the wellsprings, where they disappear.

equator/1.-world/1.1-geography.html.title: 1.1 Geography
equator/1.-world/1.1-geography.html.description:
Afarsti is the continent upon which the campaign will take place. It is a place with a deep history, a place with an innate power ingrained into every breadth of its land. Knowledge of the early days of the continent does not come easily, shrouded in mythology and kept close to the elites of society. 

The Rams are the mountain range that stretches across Afarsti. The northernmost peaks of the Rams are home to the Dailow and several native settlements. There are other continents out there, but they are exceedingly difficult to reach. Powerful spells by teams of people are needed to protect ships from the vigorous storms that surround the ocean around the continent.
There are limited trade routes from Faje to other continents, and there are certain few travellers that pass through. Commodities from other continents are extremely expensive and are held by only the most elite individuals.

equator/1.-world/1.3-magic-&-magical-bea.title: 1.3 Magic & Magical Beasts
equator/1.-world/1.3-magic-&-magical-bea.description: In the world of Equator, there is no concept of magic. Supernatural forces are not seen as other or miraculous - they simply are, just as the material is in our world. There are certain forces that are unexplainable - the supernatural power of Brun artefacts, the ability of some to use spells - but these are just as bizarre as the fact that the sun rises every day to the inhabitants of this world. There are, of course, people who seek to know the truths of the world, just as we have scientists. The laws of the universe are simply fundamentally different.It is said in Maqua mythology that the wellsprings emerged when Ramaq wandered the land and became thirsty, and the world offered her water. The Noru clan believes the wellsprings emerged when the moon was killed and its blood fell upon the world. Whatever their origin, these are sites of great power scattered about the land. The water from the springs is a potent alchemical ingredient, spell component and commodity. Bathing in the pools is known to result in madness, and drinking the water of the pools causes intense lucid dreams. It is by far the easiest to harness magical force for an average person. Most spellcasting focuses are imbued with some element from the Wellsprings, for example gems tumbled in Wellspring water over a long period of time, or a book written in ink made of Wellspring water. The Children of the Wellspring are particularly reliant on it (see 2.151). Despite its commercial potential for magic users, the Wellsprings themselves cannot be farmed very efficiently. This is due to the fact that around every Wellspring there are inevitably a variety of horrid and violent monsters. This makes Wellspring water quite expensive, and higher quality Wellspring spellcasting focuses drive a very high price. Items infused from the Wellspring directly rather than from water taken out of it are even more powerful, though their effects can be unpredictable. There are strange and miraculous creatures in Afarsti, not excluding the sentient races. Dangerous beasts roam the wilderness, claiming lives. Some creatures have been domesticated.Some especially powerful creatures’ body parts can be used as bases to use magic with. Phoenix feathers and unicorn horns, dragons claws and minotaur horns all make powerful focuses. Some mortals form bonds with certain beasts and live alongside them. Some creatures are capable of advanced thought and are incredibly powerful. These are known as great beasts. Mortals can make pacts with them, using their great power in return for something.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.10-fighte.title: 2.10 Fighter, Barbarian, Rogue, Ranger
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.10-fighte.description: The most open ended of the classes in terms of play. There have always been warriors and thieves. You could have been a Maqua soldier. You could have been a pickpocketer, scraping by in the great markets of Zaada. Most of the subclasses here fit the setting as they are mostly martial, if you have a specific subclass you are unsure of, let me know.
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.10-fighte.sourcePath: Equator/2. Class/2.1 Classes/2.10 Fighter, Barbarian, Rogue, Ranger.md

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.11-cleric.title: 2.11 Cleric
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.11-cleric.description: I prefer to see a cleric more generally as someone possessing powerful faith. This doesn't have to be in a god- it could be your unwavering faith in your nation, yourself, an object, a weapon or even just a regular person. Not that faith in a god doesn’t make an interesting character; there are various religious groups in Afarsti, or it could be more personal - a long-dead village hero that has been mythologised within your community to the point of deification.Something to note is that Afarsti doesn’t have a pantheon like the standard 5e setting, so your domain (subclass) is more about the ways that you choose to express your faith than the deity itself. Most of the ‘gods’ in Afarsti are deified historical figures, forces of nature, physical artefacts or living beings, none of which are simplified to a single domain of power (although there may be certain areas that certain deities align with more, like Ramaq with the sun).Among the Brunite, there are people who choose, or are chosen, to have a weapon as their artefact for a variety of reasons. The bond that these people share with their weapons are second to none - they become a second body, a second beating heart. These people are the Swordbrothers, a class of powerful warriors with a bond with their weapon like no other.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.12-druid..title: 2.12 Druid
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.12-druid..description:
Pretty self explanatory, where there be plants there be druids. Wild shape lore-wise is just kind of an unexplained thing, seen as a gift from the land to those who truly appreciate it. Reflavoured Circle of the Moon The Wellspring Druids are druids who protect the Wellsprings, whether they hold the belief of the Noru and see them as sacred places or simply find them beautiful.
Reflavoured Circle of the LandThese druids believe that their respective environments are as much a part of them as they are of it.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.13-paladi.title: 2.13 Paladin
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.13-paladi.description: A paladin is someone who has made a promise. Generally this means they’ve been sworn into some kind of order, to protect something, to slay something, to accomplish something. It could be expanded more widely - a promise to a loved one, a promise to yourself, a contract made out of desperation, a debt owed. Either way, there are consequences if you break this promise (Oathbreaking in the PB), but equally your goal empowers you. There are a variety of orders to join within the factions, and a lot of different promises to be made, so please let me know what you're interested in and we can talk about oath types.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.14-wizard.title: 2.14 Wizard
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.14-wizard.description: Most wizard subclasses work.‘Scalper’ is a somewhat derogatory term given to wizards who harvest magical creature’s bodies for spell components. Often carrying a butcher-shop scent, these macabre characters harness the intrinsic power of spell focuses to extract spells specific to the beast.Weaving magic into images, these wizards use illustration to cast spells with infused inks. The tradition of the cartograph originated among the Brun who had implements as their artefacts, but has since diffused across the continent.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.15-sorcer.title: 2.15 Sorcerer
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.15-sorcer.description: Will be running improved sorcerer.The Wellsprings, beautiful as they are mysterious, can be alluring to some. When young children begin to dream of the wellsprings, night after night, when they wander from their beds, when they drift towards the forest, they become known as a Child of the Wellspring, if they are ever seen again. Seemingly randomly, these children are drawn by a mysterious power to submerge themselves in the Wellspring before they turn of age. Even without knowing the way, something guides them towards one. From that day, these children are blessed with strange power and strange dreams.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.16-warloc.title: 2.16 Warlock
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.16-warloc.description: You have made a pact with one of the Great Beasts in the world. Here are some ideas, but let me know if you have a desired warlock subclass and ill see what i can do.Abandoned or lost, you found yourself alone in the wilderness as a child. The fates blessed you, then, with a saviour in a strange shape. Perhaps a fairy court took a liking to you, or a dragon happened upon you. Either way, this beast is the only family you’ve ever known. Your pact is one of reliance or love. Your life was spared in return for your servitude. Now, you exist at the whim of a great beast. You must obey its orders, or something will be taken, perhaps your life or something more. You are granted power, but your leash is short.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.17-monk.h.title: 2.17 Monk
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.17-monk.h.description: Most monk subclasses make sense, ask if unsureThe Dailow people are hardy, resourceful and desperate, and this is never more strongly reflected than in their warriors. Dailow soldiers fight bare handed, so that their weapon can never be taken away from them. There’s a rumour that Dailow soldiers are taught to fight with their legs if their arms are severed, and to fight with their teeth if their legs are removed. They are incredibly aware of their own body, able to control its flow of energy down to the sinew, and among skilled soldiers, this control extends to their mind. You could be a tried and true member of the formal militia that fiercely guards the Northern Rams, or just someone who grew up there and was taught these techniques to defend yourself.Mechanically, it will manifest as a modified version of the Way of the Open Hand (basic monk subclass) with a few tweaks to make it play more uniquely and to be more thematic.

equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.18-bard.h.title: 2.18 Bard
equator/2.-class/2.1-classes/2.18-bard.h.description: Just artists. Ask if unsure about any subclass.

equator/2.-class/2.-class.html.title: 2. Class
equator/2.-class/2.-class.html.description: These are intended to be guidelines on how a specific class might fit within the world. If you have questions about a particular subclass, please let me know. Most of these are edited versions of existing subclasses. Think of this as window shopping - if you see a subclass you like flavour-wise, tell me and I will let you know their full levelled breakdown.2.1 Classes2.2 Understanding classPeople within the world do not understand each other through the lens of class. There is no concept of fighter vs barbarian, they do not recognise the rules of the game we are playing. There is a general understanding of party balance strategically, eg. it's good to have a healer as well as someone who can do damage, and it might be good to have someone knowledgeable and wise in the world to guide the group. There are, of course, recognised ‘roles’ within society, a writer or a songstress being, rules wise, a bard. Choosing a class, for this table, should come down to thinking about a character first, thinking about where they might draw their power, and seeing which class fits that best.What this is basically saying is that these class families are as loose categories as you can make them. Do you have a character who is so self centred they believe they can do anything? They could be a cleric whose deity is themselves, and they gain their abilities through their unwavering faith like any other cleric. Colourful conflict could arise when their sense of self wavers and therefore so do their powers. Do you have a character who has lived a life of chronic pain, who is overly aware of their bodily sensations? They could be a monk, having been aware of the innermost workings of their body since they were young and learning to control its energy on a microscopic level. These categories exist to provide gameplay mechanics to your character, not as templates to limit your creativity. If you are unsure about anything, please ask!

equator/3.-race/3.2-pinchinchu.html.title: 3.2 Pinchinchu
equator/3.-race/3.2-pinchinchu.html.description: The Pinchinchu are the most populous race in Afarsti, making up the founding members of the Maquaana Empire, but also existing beyond it. They are avian in nature, but their wings have become vestigal and they can no longer fly. There are a few different types of Pinchinchu.Speed: Depends on subraceAverage height: Depends on subraceLife expectancy: 65 yearsLanguages: Maqua, one other if it makes sense Talons: You have talons that you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals 1d6 + your Strength modifier slashing damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.Variants: Height: 5’0Speed: 35ftResembles an Incan TernNative to the coasts of the Empire’s original land, the Tern is the most common of the Pinchinchu, and presently the subspecies of the God King line (though they have been other species in the past). They are nimble, social and intelligent.Pride of the Empire: +1 to Persuasion. Once per short rest, when in the sun and out of combat, regenerate 1d10+level hit points.Height: 5’9Speed: 30ftResembles any kind of PotooResidents of the jungle areas of the Empire, Potoo variant Pinchinchu are naturally nocturnal, but since their civilisation was subsumed into the empire many years ago, they have been made to comply with the sleeping habits of the rest of the continent. Oftentimes, this means that they can come across as dazed or unfocused.Arborious: +2 to Stealth checks when in woodland. Darkvision 25ftHeight: 7ftSpeed: 30ftResembles the Andean CondorTowering above its compatriots, the intimidation of the condor pinchinchu cannot be denied. With a bald head and black feathers, the enemies of the Maqua see condors in their nightmares. Wingbeat: +1 to Intimidation. As a reaction, when an enemy attacks, you can hit an enemy within 5ft with your wings, dealing 1d6+STR.

equator/3.-race/3.3-ger.html.title: 3.3 Ger
equator/3.-race/3.3-ger.html.description: Resembles a humanoid spectacled bear.The Ger are a scattered people. They often live alone in the wilderness. By no means does this make them bad company - the Ger are famed for their wisdom and storytelling. Encountering a Ger lodge when lost in the woods is the best a traveller can hope for. There are also the occasional Ger living in cities and settlements.Speed: 30ftAverage height: 6’5Life expectancy: 95 yearsLanguages: Maqua, and the language spoken in place of birthPowerful Build: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift. Durable: You have great durability. Your hit point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a level.

equator/3.-race/3.4-human.html.title: 3.4 Human
equator/3.-race/3.4-human.html.description: Humans make up the vast majority of the population of the Dailow. They are tough, fiercely faction-loyal and can be somewhat unwelcoming to outsiders. Humans are also scattered across the continent, some having been subsumed into the Maqua. Speed: 30ftAverage height: 5’5Life expectancy: 80 yearsLanguages: Bailow, MaquaSpirit: Once per short rest, when you would be reduced to 0hp or below, you are instead reduced to 1hp. Pride: During a short or long rest, you may tell a story to your compatriots, granting you and all who hear you 5 temporary hit points.

equator/3.-race/3.5-grung.html.title: 3.5 Grung
equator/3.-race/3.5-grung.html.description: These are a preexisting 5e race, I'm just including them because I think they are silly and would like to include them as NPCs. You can also be a grung. https://dnd5e.wikidot.com/lineage:grungLanguages: Maqua, AlgiaThe Grung mostly live in the Naokari Wetlands as the second most populous species. There, they mostly keep to themselves within their family groups. A lot of young Grung have left their homes to explore the world.

equator/3.-race/3.6-pluri.html.title: 3.6 Pluri
equator/3.-race/3.6-pluri.html.description: The Pluri are an amphibious human-like species that are native to the coastal regions of the Naokari Wetlands. Their distinctive shimmery skin and black eyes differentiate them from their human counterparts.Speed: 30ft, 30ft swimming speedverage height: 5’9Life expectancy: 95 yearsLanguages: Algia, MaquaAmphibious: You can breathe air and water. Aquatic: You have resistance to Cold damage. Diet: You can eat raw meat without repercussions. Tidal Flow: +1 to Insight.

equator/3.-race/3.7-brux.html.title: 3.7 Brux
equator/3.-race/3.7-brux.html.description: Flavoured wererat shifters basicallyThe Brux are the majority of the Brun, and were the founding members of the culture. They are capable of shifting their bodies from relatively human-like to a form resembling a rodent. Speed: 30ftAverage height: 5’4Life expectancy: 60 yearsLanguages: Brun, MaquaShift: Use a bonus action to shift between forms. Whilst shifted to rodent form, your Speed is increased to 35ft, and you may Dash as a bonus action. Your size is Small. You can only speak Brun. You have a +2 to Perception (Hearing) and Perception (Smell).

equator/3.-race/3.8-silt.html.title: 3.8 Silt
equator/3.-race/3.8-silt.html.description: The Silt are a reptillian race who are native to Grentia. They are cold-blooded , but not necessarily cold-hearted. They have a reputation for diplomacy and trade.Speed: 30ftAverage height: 5’2Life expectancy: 60 yearsLanguages: Maqua, GreniReptillian: You are resistant to Fire damage.Unihemispheic Sleep: During periods of sleep, you are still alert to threats. When you are going to be put to sleep magically, you may choose instead to take disadvantage on saving throws for 1d6 turns.Cunning: You gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, Deception, Arcana, History

equator/3.-race/3.9-carsa.html.title: 3.9 Carsa
equator/3.-race/3.9-carsa.html.description: The Carsa are horned humanoids native to the northernmost point of the continent, where they mostly lived in isolation until the Bailow were driven northwards. They are a hardy and resilient people, accustomed to the unforgiving terrain of the mountains.Speed: 35ftAverage height: 5’5Life expectancy: 80 yearsLanguages: Kili, Maqua, Bailow if applicable Mountain Whispers: Proficiency in Perception, +2 to Passive PerceptionClimb: You have a 25ft climbing speed.Jump: +5ft jump distance.

sam-lore/brunea.html.title: Brunea
sam-lore/brunea.html.description:
A large farming town in the north of Brun Territory. They specialise in growing maize but also farm large quantities of beans and squash. The majority of the populace are farmers who live a relatively frugal lifestyle, subsisting on their own produce as well as trade with nearby towns.
The people of Brunea are largely unaware of affairs outside of their own circles. They are not uneducated on the general geography and basic politics of Afarsti but for the most part, people here are focused on their own business, living season to season in the fields.Once every month or so, someone is found pale, collapsed, and dead on the streets of Brunea.
There's no discernible pattern, and neither chief nor tupile could find a suspect or evidence of a murder, and so over time it came to be believed that these deaths where punishment from the souls of their ancestors for not working hard enough. They believed that the bodies were found cold and pale because their blood had been taken as nourishment for the gods, quenching their thirst in the absence of adequate crop production. This belief has been manipulated by the current chief as a sort of propaganda. It has been used to convince the people to work harder, and for longer periods of time without rest, leading to a broken society with little hope for the future other than to please the apparent whims of their late parents and grandparents.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
